# `silk/cli/command`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Static descriptions of a command line: the command, its options, its positional arguments, and
its subcommands.

## When to use
Describe a type with `impl CommandLine for T`, returning a [`Command`](#Command) built with [`Opt`](#Opt), then
give the type to `silk.cli.parse.Cli.parse` or `Cli.read`.

## Details
Every operation here is `static`, so a description is a compile-time value. A description names
fields by their labels, written as string literals that the compiler checks against the type,
so `Command<Git>.make(...) |> Command.option("quiet", ...)` stops compilation at `"quiet"` when
`Git` has no field `quiet`. The field types choose how each value is read; the description only
adds names, aliases, help text, defaults, and whether a field is positional, a subcommand, or
required. A field that the description does not mention is still an option, named after its
label.

A union describes subcommands: each variant is one, named after its label in kebab case, and
its fields are that subcommand's options and arguments. A struct or variant field marked with
`Command.subcommand` holds such a union.

Import as `Command` with `import silk.cli.command { Command }`.

Public declarations: 6.

<a id="CommandLine"></a>

## `CommandLine`

```silk
pub interface CommandLine
```

A type that the command line can build: a struct of options and positional arguments, or a
union whose variants are subcommands.

### Details

`command` describes the type. The default describes nothing, so every field is an option named
after its label and every variant is a subcommand named after its label, in kebab case. Write
`impl CommandLine for T {}` to take the default, or give `command` to add names, help text, and
positional arguments.

<a id="CommandLine.command"></a>

### Operation `command`

```silk
static fn command() -> Command<Self>
```

Returns the description of the type.

<a id="Command.impl.option"></a>

### Associated function `option`

```silk
pub static fn option(
    command: Command<T>,
    field: Intrinsic.FieldName<T>,
    option: OptionSpec,
  ) -> Command<T>
```

Returns `command` with the field `field` read as a named option, described by `option`.

#### Details

`field` is checked against the fields of `T` where it is written, so a misspelled name is a
compile error at the name. For a union, `field` names a field of any of its variants.

<a id="Command.impl.arg"></a>

### Associated function `arg`

```silk
pub static fn arg(
    command: Command<T>,
    field: Intrinsic.FieldName<T>,
    argument: OptionSpec,
  ) -> Command<T>
```

Returns `command` with the field `field` read as a positional argument, described by
`argument`. Positional arguments are read in the order they are added. A `List` field takes
every remaining positional argument.

<a id="Command.impl.subcommand"></a>

### Associated function `subcommand`

```silk
pub static fn subcommand(command: Command<T>, field: Intrinsic.FieldName<T>) -> Command<T>
```

Returns `command` with the field `field` read as a subcommand. The field's type is a union
with `CommandLine`, and the command line names one of its variants in kebab case, such as
`remote` for the variant `Remote`.

<a id="Command.impl.flatten"></a>

### Associated function `flatten`

```silk
pub static fn flatten(command: Command<T>, field: Intrinsic.FieldName<T>) -> Command<T>
```

Returns `command` with the field `field` read as a group of options. The field's type is a
struct with `CommandLine`, and its options are written as options of this command, so one
group, such as the options every build command shares, is described once and used by many
commands.

#### Details

A group holds named options only: its own positional arguments or subcommands are a compile
error. Help lists the group's options among the command's own.


<a id="Opt.impl.env"></a>

### Associated function `env`

```silk
pub static fn env(option: OptionSpec, name: string<'static>) -> OptionSpec
```

Returns `option` that reads the environment variable `name` when the command line does not
give it. Only `Cli.fromHost` and `Cli.parseWith` read the environment.

<a id="Opt.impl.check"></a>

### Associated function `check`

```silk
pub static fn check<V>(option: OptionSpec, check: fn<'static>(&V) -> bool) -> OptionSpec
```

Returns `option` whose value must pass `check`, an ordinary function of the field's value,
such as `Opt.check<u32>(positive)` for a `u32` field. A value that fails it is an invalid
value; the parser calls `check` directly.
